t.6.35.1: Seeking to trace his course, that valiant and exceedingly mighty prince Rāma directed ten leaders of the monkey troops.
t.6.35.2: The two sons of Suṣeṇa, and Nīla, the bull among monkeys, and Aṅgada, the son of Vālin, and the swift and mighty Śarabha.
t.6.35.4: Those monkeys, all greatly thrilled, raised up terrible trees and entered the sky, searching through the ten directions.
t.6.35.3: The scorcher of foes gave his orders to Vinata and Jāmbavant, to the mighty Sānuprastha, and to Ṛṣabha, whose shoulders were like a bull's.
t.6.35.5: Rāvaṇi, skilled in weapons, checked the onrush of those swift ones with arrows swifter still and with a supreme weapon.
t.6.35.6: The monkeys of fearsome speed, wounded and torn all over by iron arrows, could not see him in the darkness, like the sun veiled by clouds.
t.6.35.7: Rāvaṇi, victorious in battle, drove deep into Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa themselves arrows that pierce every vital spot.
t.6.35.8: But the two heroic brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, had their bodies pierced all over without any gap by the enraged Indrajit, with serpents that had taken the form of arrows.
t.6.35.10: Then Rāvaṇi, his eyes red at the corners, resembling a heap of crushed collyrium, having become invisible, spoke these words to the two brothers.
t.6.35.9: Much blood streamed from the two of them along the channels of their wounds, and both of them shone like a pair of kiṃśuka trees in full blossom.
t.6.35.11: When he fights unseen, even Śakra, lord of the thirty gods, is unable to see him or even approach him; how much less, then, you two?
t.6.35.12: Here I stand, my soul overcome with wrath, and I shall send the two Rāghavas, shrouded in a net of arrows fletched with heron feathers, to the abode of Yama.
t.6.35.13: Having spoken thus, he pierced the two brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, knowers of dharma, with sharp arrows, and he rejoiced and roared.
t.6.35.14: Dark as a heap of crushed collyrium, he drew his mighty bow to its full stretch and in that great battle loosed terrible arrows again and again.
t.6.35.15: Then the hero, knower of the vital points, sinking his sharpened arrows into the vital points of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, roared again and again.
t.6.35.16: Bound by the binding of arrows at the forefront of battle, those two, within the mere space of a twinkling, were unable even to look up.
t.6.35.17: Then the two of them, their every limb pierced and both studded with arrow-shafts, trembled like the two banners of great Indra released from their ropes.
t.6.35.18: Those two heroes, great archers and lords of the earth, staggering and tormented by the piercing of their vital parts, fell down upon the earth.
t.6.35.19: Those two heroes lay on a hero's bed, drenched in blood, every limb bound fast by arrows, afflicted and in the utmost pain.
t.6.35.20: Indeed, there was not a finger's breadth of space on the bodies of those two, right up to the tips of their hands, that was not pierced, not torn open, and not stiffened by the straight-flying arrows.
t.6.35.22: Rāma fell first, pierced in his vital points by the arrows that Indrajit had loosed in wrath, Indrajit by whom Śakra himself had once been vanquished.
t.6.35.21: But the two of them, struck down by the cruel rākṣasa who could take any form at will, poured forth blood profusely, like two springs pouring out water.
t.6.35.23: He pierced him with nārācas and half-nārācas, with bhallas and añjalikas too, with vatsadantas, siṃhadaṃṣṭras and kṣuras as well.
t.6.35.25: Seeing Rāma, that bull among men, fallen there amid the shower of arrows, Lakṣmaṇa lost all hope of life.
t.6.35.24: He lay upon the bed of heroes, clasping his unstrung bow, its handgrip shattered, bent in three places and adorned with gold.
t.6.35.26: The monkeys, gathered together with the son of Vāyu at their head, surrounded and stood around those two heroes, who lay bound and fallen; and, stricken with grief, they sank into the deepest despair.
